title: Zero to Unbeatable
tagline: Watch real reinforcement learning go from random moves to provably unbeatable
card_blurb: Play tic-tac-toe against an AI that has played zero games — and beat it easily. Train it in three-second bursts and play again, era by era, until you cannot beat it and the app proves you never will. The only thing that changed is a list of numbers.
description: **Zero to Unbeatable** — a single-file, phone-first demo of how machines learn. Tabular reinforcement learning that starts from zero knowledge and plays uniformly at random, trained in visible 5,000-game bursts between which the student plays it; frozen eras with per-era scoreboards, a brain inspector that overlays the learned value of every square, a "what it learned" card with before/after heatmaps of landmark positions, and an ending the app proves by searching every reachable game line rather than sampling. A second act trains it on nine boards at once — a mark per turn on any unfinished board, first to five boards — to show what breaks when the world gets bigger: on one board a position recurs 10x per training burst, on nine it recurs 1.06x, so no table could ever learn it. No network, no AI service, nothing baked in. Includes a printable demo guide.
